ocr.notes: Most readable; Allen's letter and later paragraphs have many errors (e.g. 'Domuey' for Looney, garbled lines near the end).

title.suggested: Allen Answers the Republican on Coburn as the Hogan Fight Nears

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Democrat previewed the Allen-Hogan fight set for the 28th and printed a letter from Tom Allen denying the Republican's claim he feared Joe Coburn, offering $500 to whip any man in the world.

metadata.notes: Running head reads 'The St. Louis Democrat: St. Louis, Friday, October 24, 1873'; masthead 'Daily Democrat'. Pre-1875 merger.

facts.fact: Allen was training for the Hogan fight at the Eight-Mile House, St. Louis County; his letter was dated from the Mount Olive House
places: Mount Olive House, St. Louis County

facts.fact: Allen wrote to the Democrat denying the Republican's claim that he would not fight Joe Coburn, saying he had challenged Coburn again and again without reply
facts.quote: Now the sporting men of St. Louis know that I have challenged Coburn again and again, and never got any reply.

facts.fact: Allen offered $500 that he could whip any man in the world, including Joe Coburn
facts.quote: there are $500 at my house that say that I can whip any man in the world, as well as that newspaper fighter, Joe Coburn. I never sent a challenge in my life that I did not back with my money.

facts.fact: A New York dispatch said Joe Coburn would decline all challenges, having resolved after his Mace match not to enter the ring again

notes: Letter signed 'Tom Allen, Champion'. Arthur Chambers to act as one of Allen's seconds.
